clue.text: Magic word receiving low frequency and none other

indicators.note: a thing receiving something takes it inside itself, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: 'open sesame' is the magic password in Ali Baba
the standard abbreviation for low frequency

explanation.surface: A conjuror's spell picks up a low hum and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open sesame' is the password in the tale of Ali Baba, which makes it a magic word; 'none other' is the definition, an archaic way of saying the very same.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfsame means exactly the identical one, so it describes the very thing and no different item.

clue.text: Parting of the ways when Mao's lost taste for torture

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so these letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a liking for pain inflicted on oneself
the Chinese leader's name, as letters to be taken out

explanation.surface: A split arises when the Chairman gives up his liking for cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: The M, A and O are removed from scattered positions in the longer word, leaving SCHISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division within a group, a separation into factions going different ways.

clue.text: Soldiers charge onto stage

indicators.note: one piece placed onto another in a down entry is attached after it

parts.note: a stage of a journey or race is a leg
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: Troops storm the theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests an attack but is the charged particle; 'stage' is a section of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit, so the word stands for a large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Support for victims of the rack?

definitions.text: Support for victims of the rack?

parts.note: surface reading: a frame for carrying the injured
setter's reading: the rack is a torture device that stretches its victims

explanation.walkthrough: The rack lengthens its victims; the answer is both the thing that does the lengthening and the frame that carries casualties.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names a carrying frame for the sick and injured, and also anything that elongates, as the rack does.

clue.text: Acquisitive type putting cash back into the kitty for masseuse

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so this pairs with the following preposition

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: putting money back makes it run the other way in this down entry

parts.note: the Japanese currency
a masseuse rubs people

explanation.surface: A greedy person returns money to the pot to pay for a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a pool of money, but here it is a cat; mog or moggy is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-grubber is a greedy person obsessed with getting wealth, which is someone eager to acquire.

clue.text: The revolution sets on Switzerland

indicators.note: one piece sits on, that is next to, the other, so the two are joined end to end

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: An uprising takes hold in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: PUTSCH is itself a Swiss-German word, which makes the Switzerland reference doubly neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, a kind of violent political upheaval.

clue.text: Instrument binding a Pole to Russian rule

indicators.note: an instrument binding things holds them tightly within it

parts.note: short for ukulele
taken as written
S for the South Pole

explanation.surface: A legal instrument ties a Polish citizen to Russian domination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' reads as a legal document and 'Pole' as a Polish person; they are a ukulele and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict issued by the Russian tsar, a decree with the force of law.

clue.text: Showed allegiance to unconventional member of orchestra

parts.note: to side with someone is to support them
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: Someone backed an eccentric orchestral player.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the old British adjective for strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A side drum is the snare drum, one of the percussion instruments that makes up part of an orchestra.

clue.text: Sharpen up by repeating note on buzzer

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the musical note E, given twice

explanation.surface: Improve your sound by playing the same note on a buzzer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' looks like a gadget but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeybee is an insect that famously makes a humming noise in flight, so it is a creature that buzzes.

clue.text: Senior office is doubly malodorous

parts.note: meat that is high smells bad
rank also means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A top job turns out to stink twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' asks for two different words meaning smelly, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A high rank is an elevated position in a hierarchy, such as a senior post or office.

clue.text: The Virgin Soldiers get help

indicators.note: the soldiers get, that is take in, the other piece so it sits inside them

parts.note: soldiers are men in crossword shorthand
aid is a synonym of help

explanation.surface: Echoing the novel The Virgin Soldiers, troops receive assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an unmarried young woman, traditionally a virgin, as in the Virgin Mary's title.

clue.text: Grave words spoken when a man's digits get hold of tree

indicators.note: digits that get hold of something grip it, so it ends up inside them

parts.note: as means when
a man is, contracted to he's
toes are the digits of the foot
the ash tree

explanation.surface: Words said at a graveside when a man's fingers grasp wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' means serious on the surface but is a burial plot here; the phrase comes from the funeral service.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is part of the burial service in the Book of Common Prayer, spoken as the coffin is lowered.

clue.text: A drink that can be relied on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong dark beer such as porter

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing something that can be relied on

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one drink you can trust; it is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a dark beer, and as an adjective it means firm, brave and staunch, like a dependable friend.

clue.text: Not long ago an article of the Beatles' faith?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the day before today, or recently

definitions.text: an article of the Beatles' faith?
definitions.note: a cryptic second definition naming the song title
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Beatles song with the line 'I believe in' this day

explanation.walkthrough: In the Beatles song the singer says 'I believe in yesterday', so the word is something they hold as a belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday refers to the recent past, and is also a famous Beatles song whose lyric professes belief in it.

clue.text: School book on building

indicators.note: one word placed on another is simply set alongside it to form the whole

parts.note: to charter a plane or boat is to book it
a house is a building

explanation.surface: A school textbook about architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is a verb here, to hire, not a volume. Charterhouse is an English public (fee-paying) school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is the name of a well-known independent boarding school in England, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: Suggestion about money-spinning at the Sign of the Horse

indicators.note: a suggestion about something wraps around it

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion
oof is old slang for money
public relations, the business of spin

explanation.surface: A tip about making a profit at a pub called the Horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign of the Horse' sounds like a pub name; a pub sign hangs outside an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofprint is the mark left on the ground by a horse, evidence that the animal has passed by.

clue.text: A firm absorbing a firm absorbing university town in Mexico

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a company absorbing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: company
taken as written
public limited company
U for university

explanation.surface: Corporate mergers in which one firm swallows another that has taken over a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Both familiar abbreviations for a business are needed, the short one outside and the public limited one inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort city on Mexico's Pacific coast, so it is a Mexican town.

clue.text: Group dropping both ends of fellows' symbol

indicators.note: dropping both ends means the very first and very last letters go

parts.note: fellows are men, with the possessive
an emblem is a symbol

explanation.surface: A club gives up the two ends of its members' badge.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the outer M's of the joined phrase are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a set of musicians or performers working together, which is a kind of group.

clue.text: Offering to be funny, but not ironic

indicators.note: letters that are made funny are made odd, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone's contribution is meant to be humorous without being sarcastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the remainder reads like advice to a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A contribution is something given, such as a donation or a piece submitted, which is what an offering is.

clue.text: Balk at hovel where I cut myself

parts.note: a sty is a filthy dwelling

indicators.note: a letter that cuts a word splits it apart and sits inside

parts.note: me stands for myself
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recoiling at a shack where someone injured themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balk at' looks like the definition with a preposition, but the definition is 'Balk', a verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, just as to balk someone means to hinder or frustrate them.

clue.text: It's highly desirable to secure space for general meeting

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast inside

parts.note: a plum job is a highly desirable one
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Getting a room booked for the general meeting is important.
explanation.walkthrough: An en space is a printer's unit of spacing, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a meeting attended by all members of an assembly, a full general session.

clue.text: State in which bird has forewarning of strange occurrences

indicators.note: the state is a place in which the other parts are found, so they go inside it

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania
a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: In some state a bird senses that weird events are coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' joins the bird to its forewarning, and both sit inside the abbreviated US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable events or facts, especially unusual or unexplained happenings.

clue.text: Arab will be back in a tick

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: 'in a mo', a moment, means very soon

explanation.surface: An Arab promises to return shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will be back in a tick' reads as a promise to return; 'back' turns 'in a mo' around.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, a country on the Arabian peninsula, so an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Friend welcoming alien with a term of endearment

indicators.note: a friend welcoming someone lets them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pal is a synonym of friend
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A friend greets a visitor from space affectionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petal' is a fond form of address in northern England, like 'love' or 'pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petal is used affectionately to address someone dear, especially in the north of England, so it is an endearment.

clue.text: Students taking a degree involving one type of sound

indicators.note: a degree involving something has it within, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: L for learner, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: the students taking the rest hold it between them, so their two letters sit at either end

parts.note: taken as written
Bachelor of Arts
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Students pursue a degree that involves one kind of phonetic sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The two learners' L's go one at each end, around A plus BA with I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A labial is a consonant made with the lips, such as p, b or m, a category of speech sound.

clue.text: Detective admits woman as spokesperson

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Charlie Chan, the fictional detective
a woman's name

explanation.surface: An investigator confesses a woman acted as his mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admits' looks like confesses but means takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman leads a committee or company and often speaks publicly for it, acting as its representative voice.

clue.text: A trap that almost ensnared Tatiana?

definitions.text: A trap that almost ensnared Tatiana?

parts.note: a means one
a gin is a snare for game

explanation.surface: A snare nearly caught a Russian heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Pushkin's Eugene Onegin, Tatiana falls for the hero, who rejects her; the whole clue describes him as a near-trap for her.
explanation.definitionFit: Onegin is the title character of Pushkin's verse novel, the man whom Tatiana loves and nearly gives herself to.

clue.text: Differing in doctrine, but not in heat here

definitions.text: Differing in doctrine, but not in heat here

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: an ism is a doctrine or belief system
other means different

explanation.surface: Holding different beliefs, though agreeing on temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Places along this line may differ in every way except temperature, which is why 'but not in heat' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a map joining places with the same temperature, so they differ in other ways only.
